subject: Renewal & mid-contract uplift — packaging options and co-term path

Subject: Renewal & mid-contract uplift — packaging options and co-term path

Hi Emma,

Hope you're well. I dug into Mira's Q3 usage (attached) and can see the burst you mentioned — looks like a ~35% step-up in inference volume vs. our baseline. Ahead of your renewal next March we can approach this in a couple of clean ways; I wanted to outline two pragmatic paths so procurement has clear options: 

Option 1 — One-time top-up (fastest):
- Add a temporary top-up bucket for the remainder of this term to cover the extra usage.
- Pro-rata invoice for the top-up; provisioning immediate.
- We can offer a 12% partner discount on the top-up if PO is in by 11/30.

Option 2 — Annualize the uplift (preferred for predictability):
- Convert the observed uplift into an annualized committed add-on and co-term it with your existing renewal on 2027-03-31.
- Blended pricing across current term + next year; we can extend an 18% discount if amendment is signed by 11/30 and commit volumes are agreed.

A few notes:
- Option 2 gives you predictability and unit-cost reduction; Option 1 minimizes legal/contract work and gets capacity quickly.
- We can split billing over multiple invoices for cashflow if helpful.
- If procurement needs we can include a short exec summary and the draft amendment for legal.

I attached the Q3 usage CSV for your team; looping in Lauren on billing and Ben on pricing to put flesh on the numbers. What timeline does procurement have for a PO?

Thanks — happy to jump on a 20-min call to walk options with finance/legal.

Best,
Dylan Brooks
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Quick commercials below (baseline numbers pulled from the attached usage; I rounded for readability). All numbers in USD.

Assumptions: baseline monthly spend ~ $48k, Q3 spike suggests incremental monthly consumption of ~$16.8k (35%). Remaining term: 4.5 months until 2027-03-31.

Option A — One-time top-up (fast provision)
- Add one-time top-up capacity to cover incremental usage for remainder of term: incremental total = $16.8k * 4.5 = $75.6k
- Apply discount: 12% partner discount = $9.1k off -> net = $66.5k
- Invoicing: can split into 2 invoices (50/50) with 30-day terms to ease cashflow.
- Notes: No contractual co-term; renewal remains unchanged.

Option B — Annualize & co-term to 2027-03-31 then renew as a larger base
- Convert uplift to annual add-on: annualized uplift (projected) = incremental monthly $16.8k * 12 = $201.6k
- Blended approach: charge remaining months at pro-rata + start of new year at full rate; for comparison to Option A I show net-first-year impact.
- Discount: 18% if amendment signed & countersigned by 11/30 -> annual net = $165.3k (approx)
- Additional flexibility: 6-month payment split available; SLA unchanged unless security requests specific changes.

Commercial tradeoffs:
- Option A is lower legal friction and faster provisioning; Option B reduces unit cost and is cleaner for forecasting.

I attached a light Draft_Amendment_Mira.docx that formalizes Option B language and gives a sign-and-return path. If procurement needs, we can convert the numbers into a one-page executive summary.

Ben Carter
Senior Pricing Manager, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com

- Can you produce a one-page exec summary that lists: (1) net-first-year cost, (2) billing cadence, (3) what changes (if any) to SLA/data handling — we need plain bullets for our finance/legal gate.

If you can send the finalized amendment + exec summary today or tomorrow we’ll queue legal review.

Best,
Emma
